subproblem.title: Countable compact exhaustion: swapping 'for all compact K ⊆ U' with 'for a.e. t'
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and (F_t)_{t∈ℝ} a family of set functions F_t : 𝒫(ℝ^P) → [0, ∞], each monotone (A ⊆ B ⇒ F_t(A) ≤ F_t(B)). Assume that for every compact K ⊆ U, F_t(K) ≠ ∞ for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ: F_t(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (F : ℝ → Set (Euclid P) → ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → (∀ t, Monotone (F t)) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ᵐ t, F t K ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → F t K ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 0(d) (compact exhaustion K_1 ⊆ K_2 ⊆ … of U, every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i) and Step 2, third bullet (for t ∈ G₁ and compact K ⊆ U take K ⊆ K_i), with the countable intersection of Step 2, second bullet.

1. Exhausting compacts. For i ∈ ℕ let T_i := thickening (1/(i+1)) Uᶜ = {y : ∃ z ∉ U, dist(y, z) < 1/(i+1)} (open; empty when U = ℝ^P), and K_i := B̄(0, i) ∖ T_i. K_i is a closed subset of the compact ball B̄(0, i), hence compact ((isCompact_closedBall 0 (i : ℝ)).diff isOpen_thickening).
2. K_i ⊆ U. Let x ∈ K_i and suppose x ∉ U. Since 1/(i+1) > 0, Uᶜ ⊆ T_i (self_subset_thickening), so x ∈ T_i, contradicting x ∈ K_i. Hence x ∈ U.
3. Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i. Since K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 with thickening δ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open). K is bounded, so K ⊆ B̄(0, R) for some R (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Choose i₁ ∈ ℕ with R ≤ i₁ (exists_nat_ge) and i₂ ∈ ℕ with 1/(i₂+1) < δ (exists_nat_one_div_lt); let i := max(i₁, i₂). Let x ∈ K.
   (a) x ∈ B̄(0, i), since B̄(0, R) ⊆ B̄(0, i₁) ⊆ B̄(0, i).
   (b) x ∉ T_i: otherwise there is y ∉ U with dist(x, y) < 1/(i+1) ≤ 1/(i₂+1) < δ (mem_thickening_iff). Then dist(y, x) < δ with x ∈ K, so y ∈ thickening δ K ⊆ U, a contradiction.
   Hence K ⊆ K_i.
4. Countable intersection. By hypothesis and steps 1–2, for each i, F_t(K_i) ≠ ∞ for a.e. t. Since ℕ is countable, for a.e. t this holds for all i simultaneously (ae_all_iff).
5. Fix such a t and a compact K ⊆ U. By step 3 choose i with K ⊆ K_i. By monotonicity F_t(K) ≤ F_t(K_i) < ∞, so F_t(K) ≠ ∞ (ne_top_of_le_ne_top). ∎

Monotone (F t) applied to K ⊆ K_i gives F t K ≤ F t K_i.]

  let Kn : ℕ → Set (Euclid P) := fun i => closedBall 0 i \ thickening (1 / ((i : ℝ) + 1)) Uᶜ
  have hKc : ∀ i, IsCompact (Kn i) := fun i =>
    (isCompact_closedBall 0 (i : ℝ)).diff isOpen_thickening
  have hKU : ∀ i, Kn i ⊆ U := by
    intro i x hx
    by_contra hxU
    exact hx.2 (self_subset_thickening (by positivity) _ hxU)
  have hcover : ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ i, K ⊆ Kn i := by
    intro K hKc' hKU'
    obtain ⟨δ, hδ, hδK⟩ := hKc'.exists_thickening_subset_open hU hKU'
    obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hKc'.isBounded.subset_closedBall 0
    obtain ⟨i₁, hi₁⟩ := exists_nat_ge R
    obtain ⟨i₂, hi₂⟩ := exists_nat_one_div_lt hδ
    refine ⟨max i₁ i₂, fun x hx => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
    · exact closedBall_subset_closedBall (hi₁.trans (by exact_mod_cast le_max_left i₁ i₂)) (hR hx)
    · intro hxt
      rw [mem_thickening_iff] at hxt
      obtain ⟨y, hyU, hxy⟩ := hxt
      have hlt : (1 : ℝ) / ((max i₁ i₂ : ℕ) + 1) ≤ 1 / ((i₂ : ℝ) + 1) := by
        gcongr; exact_mod_cast le_max_right i₁ i₂
      have hy : y ∈ thickening δ K := by
        rw [mem_thickening_iff]
        exact ⟨x, hx, by rw [dist_comm]; linarith⟩
      exact hyU (hδK hy)
  have hall : ∀ᵐ t, ∀ i, F t (Kn i) ≠ ∞ := ae_all_iff.mpr fun i => hK _ (hKc i) (hKU i)
  filter_upwards [hall] with t ht K hKc' hKU'
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hcover K hKc' hKU'

Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some K_i (positive margin δ from IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open, plus boundedness).
ae_all_iff over i ∈ ℕ: for a.e. t, F_t(K_i) ≠ ∞ for all i.
Monotonicity transfers finiteness from K_i to any compact K ⊆ K_i.

subproblem.title: Co-area transfer of almost-everywhere properties to almost every slice
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, (ν_t)_{t∈ℝ} a family of measures on ℝ^P, and w : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] any function. Assume the co-area identity: for every Borel φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], the function t ↦ ∫ φ dν_t is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_ℝ (∫ φ dν_t) dt = ∫ w·φ dμ (lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞]). Then for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds μ-a.e.: for Lebesgue-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, p(x) holds for ν_t-a.e. x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : ℝ → Measure (Euclid P)) (w : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (p : Euclid P → Prop), (∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t)) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t) = ∫⁻ x, w x * φ x ∂μ) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ᵐ x ∂(ν t), p x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (transfer of null sets to slices, via (G3) with φ = 1_Z and lintegral_eq_zero_iff'), stated for an abstract co-area identity.

1. Null hull. Let N := {x : ¬p(x)}. The hypothesis ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x says μ(N) = 0 (ae_iff). Let Z := toMeasurable μ N. Then Z is Borel (measurableSet_toMeasurable), N ⊆ Z (subset_toMeasurable) and μ(Z) = μ(N) = 0 (measure_toMeasurable).
2. Co-area with an indicator. φ := 1_Z (Z.indicator 1) is Borel and [0, ∞]-valued (measurable_one.indicator). By the co-area hypothesis, F(t) := ∫ 1_Z dν_t is a.e.-measurable on ℝ and ∫_ℝ F(t) dt = ∫ w·1_Z dμ.
3. The right side vanishes. Since μ(Z) = 0, μ-a.e. x lies outside Z (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem), and for such x, w(x)·1_Z(x) = w(x)·0 = 0. So w·1_Z = 0 μ-a.e., and ∫ w·1_Z dμ = ∫ 0 dμ = 0 (lintegral_congr_ae, lintegral_zero).
4. Hence ∫_ℝ F(t) dt = 0. As F is a.e.-measurable, lintegral_eq_zero_iff' gives F = 0 Lebesgue-a.e. on ℝ.
5. Fix t with F(t) = 0. Since Z is measurable, F(t) = ∫ 1_Z dν_t = ν_t(Z) (lintegral_indicator_one). So ν_t(Z) = 0, i.e. ν_t-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ Z (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).
6. For such x we have x ∉ N, because N ⊆ Z; that is, p(x) holds (by contradiction: ¬p(x) would give x ∈ N ⊆ Z).
7. Combining 4–6: for Lebesgue-a.e. t, p(x) holds for ν_t-a.e. x. ∎
[Lean hints (all verified to exist at mathlib 25730c7c): measurableSet_toMeasurable, subset_toMeasurable, measure_toMeasurable, ae_iff, measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem, lintegral_congr_ae, lintegral_zero, lintegral_eq_zero_iff', lintegral_indicator_one. The hypothesis is only used with φ = Z.indicator 1. w need not be measurable.]

theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_si_coarea_ae_transfer : ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : ℝ → Measure (Euclid P)) (w : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (p : Euclid P → Prop), (∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t)) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t) = ∫⁻ x, w x * φ x ∂μ) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p x) → ∀ᵐ t, ∀ᵐ x ∂(ν t), p x := by
  intro P μ ν w p hco hp
  set Z := toMeasurable μ {x | ¬ p x} with hZ
  have hZm : MeasurableSet Z := measurableSet_toMeasurable _ _
  have hμZ : μ Z = 0 := by rw [hZ, measure_toMeasurable]; exact ae_iff.mp hp
  obtain ⟨hae, heq⟩ := hco (Z.indicator 1) (measurable_one.indicator hZm)
  have hzero : ∫⁻ x, w x * Z.indicator 1 x ∂μ = 0 := by
    refine (lintegral_congr_ae ?_).trans lintegral_zero
    have : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∉ Z := measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem.mp hμZ
    filter_upwards [this] with x hx
    simp [indicator_of_notMem hx]
  rw [hzero, lintegral_eq_zero_iff' hae] at heq
  filter_upwards [heq] with t ht
  have hνZ : ν t Z = 0 := by
    have := ht
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply] at this
    rwa [lintegral_indicator_one hZm] at this
  filter_upwards [measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem.mp hνZ] with x hx
  by_contra hpx
  exact hx (subset_toMeasurable μ {x | ¬ p x} hpx)
proof_key_steps: Take the Borel μ-null hull Z := toMeasurable μ {¬p} ⊇ {¬p}.
Apply the co-area identity to φ = 1_Z: ∫_ℝ ν_t(Z) dt = ∫ w·1_Z dμ = 0 because 1_Z = 0 μ-a.e.
By lintegral_eq_zero_iff' (a.e.-measurability is part of the hypothesis), ν_t(Z) = 0 for a.e. t.
For such t, ν_t-a.e. x lies outside Z ⊇ {¬p}, so p(x) holds.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type agree. The measurable null hull, indicator identity and a.e.-measurable zero-lintegral argument prove transfer for arbitrary predicates. No measurability of w or p is needed, and no circular dependency occurs.

subproblem.title: Signed co-area identity: integrability of slice integrals and Fubini-type formula for real integrands
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P, (ν_t)_{t∈ℝ} a family of measures on ℝ^P, and w : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] Borel. Assume the co-area identity: for every Borel φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫ φ dν_t is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure and ∫_ℝ (∫ φ dν_t) dt = ∫ w·φ dμ (lower integrals). Let q : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel with ∫ w·|q| dμ < ∞ (lower integral of w(x)·‖q(x)‖ₑ). Then t ↦ ∫ q dν_t (Bochner integral; it is 0 when q is not ν_t-integrable) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ, and ∫_ℝ (∫ q dν_t) dt = ∫ w̄·q dμ, where w̄(x) := w(x) as a real number (ENNReal.toReal, so w̄ = 0 where w = ∞).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : ℝ → Measure (Euclid P)) (w : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (q : Euclid P → ℝ), (∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ → AEMeasurable (fun t => ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t)) ∧ ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ x, φ x ∂(ν t) = ∫⁻ x, w x * φ x ∂μ) → Measurable w → Measurable q → ∫⁻ x, w x * ‖q x‖ₑ ∂μ ≠ ∞ → Integrable (fun t => ∫ x, q x ∂(ν t)) ∧ ∫ t, ∫ x, q x ∂(ν t) = ∫ x, (w x).toReal * q x ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 7, bullet 'Co-area' (apply (G3) to q̃⁺ and q̃⁻ and subtract the two finite identities; real integrals from lintegrals by integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part / integral_toReal), and the measurability/integrability argument of parent Step 6, stated for an abstract co-area identity.

1. Positive and negative parts. Put q⁺(x) := ofReal(q(x)) and q⁻(x) := ofReal(−q(x)) in [0, ∞]. Both are Borel (Measurable.ennreal_ofReal applied to q and −q), and so is |q| = ‖q‖ₑ (Measurable.enorm). For real r, ofReal(r) ≤ ofReal|r| = ‖r‖ₑ and ofReal(−r) ≤ ofReal|r| = ‖r‖ₑ (ofReal_norm, Real.norm_eq_abs, le_abs_self, neg_le_abs); hence q⁺ ≤ ‖q‖ₑ and q⁻ ≤ ‖q‖ₑ pointwise.
2. Co-area for the three nonnegative functions. Apply the hypothesis to φ = q⁺, q⁻ and ‖q‖ₑ. With F^±(t) := ∫ q^± dν_t and A(t) := ∫ ‖q‖ₑ dν_t, the functions F⁺, F⁻, A are a.e.-measurable on ℝ and
   ∫_ℝ F^± dt = ∫ w·q^± dμ ≤ ∫ w·‖q‖ₑ dμ < ∞ (lintegral_mono with mul_le_mul_right of step 1),  ∫_ℝ A dt = ∫ w·‖q‖ₑ dμ < ∞.
3. Integrability on a.e. slice. By ae_lt_top' (A a.e.-measurable, ∫ A < ∞), A(t) < ∞ for a.e. t. For such t, q is ν_t-integrable: it is Borel (hence a.e.-strongly measurable) and has finite integral ∫ ‖q‖ₑ dν_t = A(t) < ∞. For these t, integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part gives ∫ q dν_t = F⁺(t).toReal − F⁻(t).toReal. Hence t ↦ ∫ q dν_t agrees Lebesgue-a.e. with G(t) := F⁺(t).toReal − F⁻(t).toReal.
4. Integrability in t and value of the left side. F^± are a.e.-measurable with finite lintegral, so t ↦ F^±(t).toReal are Lebesgue integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top), and ∫_ℝ F^±(t).toReal dt = (∫_ℝ F^± dt).toReal (integral_toReal, using F^± < ∞ a.e. from ae_lt_top'). subproblem.title: Strongly measurable slice orientation ζ' = ζ ∘ (ν♭∧·), ν = g/|g| (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_{n+1}(ℝ^P) be strongly measurable, where Λ_k(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P k is the space of continuous linear functionals on k-covectors (operator norm), and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel. For v ∈ ℝ^P and an n-covector α write v♭∧α := alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α), the (n+1)-covector (v♭∧α)(v₀, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨v, v_i⟩ α(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n). Then there is a strongly measurable ζ' : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) such that for all x ∈ ℝ^P and all n-covectors α: (a) ζ'(x)(α) = ζ(x)((|g(x)|⁻¹ g(x))♭∧α) (with 0⁻¹ = 0); (b) |g(x)|·ζ'(x)(α) = ζ(x)(g(x)♭∧α); (c) |ζ(x)(g(x)♭∧α)| ≤ (n+1)·‖ζ(x)‖·|g(x)|·‖α‖ (operator norms).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (n + 1)) (g : Euclid P → Euclid P), StronglyMeasurable ζ → Measurable g → ∃ ζ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P n, StronglyMeasurable ζ' ∧ (∀ x (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ζ' x α = ζ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (‖g x‖⁻¹ • g x)).smulRight α))) ∧ (∀ x (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖g x‖ * ζ' x α = ζ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (g x)).smulRight α))) ∧ ∀ x (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (g x)).smulRight α))| ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * ‖ζ x‖ * ‖g x‖ * ‖α‖

Source: parent Step 3 (definition of ξ̃ = ξ₀ ∘ (ν♭∧·), its strong measurability via the continuous map Ξ(ζ, v) = ζ ∘L (α ↦ v♭∧α) on MultiVector P (n+1) × ℝ^P, and the linearity identity |g|·ξ̃(α) = ξ₀(g♭∧α)), together with the bound ‖v♭∧α‖ ≤ (n+1)|v|‖α‖ of parent Step 7.

1. The wedge pairing is bilinear. Let B(v, α) := v♭∧α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) for (v, α) ∈ ℝ^P × Covector(ℝ^P, n). B is additive and ℝ-homogeneous in v and in α. Indeed innerSL ℝ is linear in v (map_add, map_smul); c ↦ c.smulRight α and α ↦ c.smulRight α are linear (check after ext y: (c.smulRight α) y = c(y) • α, then add_smul / smul_add / smul_smul); and alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and homogeneous (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add, alternatizeUncurryFin_smul). In Lean: rewrite with ← alternatizeUncurryFin_add / ← alternatizeUncurryFin_smul, then congr 1, ext y, simp [add_smul, smul_smul].
2. The wedge bound. For all v, α: ‖v♭∧α‖ ≤ (n+1)·‖(innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α‖ = (n+1)·‖innerSL ℝ v‖·‖α‖ = (n+1)·|v|·‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le, ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply, innerSL_apply_norm).
3. Steps 1–2 make B a bounded bilinear map (IsBoundedBilinearMap ℝ B, with bound constant n+1 > 0: ‖B(v, α)‖ ≤ (n+1)·|v|·‖α‖). Let A := B.toContinuousLinearMap : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] (Covector n →L[ℝ] Covector (n+1)) (IsBoundedBilinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap), so A(v)(α) = v♭∧α (definitionally, by rfl).
   [Lean warning: do not build A with ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightL or ContinuousLinearMap.compL: the instance TopologicalSpace (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] Euclid P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n) fails to synthesize. The route of step 3 (an IsBoundedBilinearMap structure written field by field: add_left, smul_left, add_right, smul_right, bound) is verified to work.]
4. Ξ is continuous. Define Ξ : MultiVector P (n+1) × ℝ^P → MultiVector P n by Ξ(ζ₀, v) := ζ₀ ∘L A(v). Composition (f, h) ↦ f ∘L h is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_comp), hence continuous, and p ↦ (p.1, A(p.2)) is continuous (continuous_fst.prodMk (A.continuous.comp continuous_snd)). So Ξ is continuous.
5. Definition and measurability of ζ'. ν(x) := |g(x)|⁻¹ g(x) is Borel (hg.norm.inv.smul hg), hence strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable; ℝ^P is second countable). Then x ↦ (ζ(x), ν(x)) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.prodMk), and ζ'(x) := Ξ(ζ(x), ν(x)) is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable).
6. (a) holds by definition: ζ'(x)(α) = ζ(x)(A(ν(x))(α)) = ζ(x)(ν(x)♭∧α).
7. (b). If g(x) = 0: the left side is 0·ζ'(x)(α) = 0, and A(0) = 0 (map_zero), so the right side is ζ(x)(0) = 0. If g(x) ≠ 0: by linearity of A and of ζ(x), ζ'(x)(α) = ζ(x)(A(|g(x)|⁻¹ • g(x))(α)) = |g(x)|⁻¹ · ζ(x)(A(g(x))(α)) (map_smul, smul_apply, smul_eq_mul); multiplying by |g(x)| and using |g(x)|·|g(x)|⁻¹ = 1 (mul_inv_cancel₀, norm_ne_zero_iff) gives (b).
8. (c). With β := g(x)♭∧α = A(g(x))(α): |ζ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖ζ(x)‖·‖β‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm) ≤ ‖ζ(x)‖·(n+1)·|g(x)|·‖α‖ by step 2; rearrange (ring). ∎
